still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.

The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels, and Congress has still not enacted the CBO-scored permanent Medicare obesity benefit. Medicare reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk codes.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 31.5% ever-used minus 23.0% current leaves 8.5% of adults who used the drugs and are off now. 47% of ever-users have cycled, or 14.8 points. About 12.6 points are current users on at least their second course (~55% of current users), and ~2.2 points cycled and are off again. The other ~6.3 points stopped once and have not restarted. That fits one-year persistence near one-third and 36–47% restarting within a year, compounded over a larger base. Ever-use rose 6.0 points, inside the 8.4-point cap. Age check: weights 0.20/0.33/0.24/0.23 × 12/21.5/31/26.5 = 2.40+7.10+7.44+6.10 = 23.0. 23.0% of ~270M adults is ~62M users. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare ~23% (~14.5M, including ~1.5M under-65 disability beneficiaries; dementia-risk route ~6.5M, up from 1.6M after the Jul 2031 label extension); Medicaid ~12% (~7.5M, 21 states now cover weight-loss use); HRSA free provision at health centres ~6% (~3.5M). Public payers total ~41% (~25.5M) and are now the largest single payer group. Commercial ~22% (~13.5M, of whom ~5.0M are in metabolic tracks). Legitimate cash ~23% (~14.5M). Gray market ~14% (~8.5M: ~3.5M compounded 503A/telehealth 'personalised' product, ~3.0M imported Indian vials, ~2.0M counterfeit pens and research peptides). Sum: 14.5+7.5+3.5+13.5+14.5+8.5 = 62M. 65+ users ≈ 26.5% × ~63M ≈ 16.7M, of whom ~13M are on Medicare and ~3.7M are on cash, retiree plans or gray product. The bottom third rose 12 → 20, almost entirely through HRSA and new Medicaid states. The top-to-bottom gap narrowed (26 vs 20), but what each tier takes diverged (see access). About 4.5M current users have a BMI under 27 and take low-dose orals or compounded product for 'metabolic health' or longevity, nearly all cash or gray, ~two-thirds in the top income third. Adult obesity ~32.8%. About 20% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug. Pediatric: ~1.4% of under-18s; ~2.9% of 12–17s; ~0.35% of 6–11s, still mostly generic liraglutide, now also reachable through Medicaid EPSDT in the new-coverage states.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~14.5M) reaches users through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes. Since the Jul 2031 tirzepatide label extension, the dementia-risk code covers adults 60+ with obesity without CVD, and CMS's Part D guidance limits prior authorisation to a BMI and age check. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 14.5M × ~$235 average net/month × 12 ≈ $40.9B a year gross Part D incretin spend, of which the dementia route is 6.5M × ~$245 × 12 ≈ $19.1B. Medicaid (~7.5M, 21 states covering weight loss after the Mar 2031 package raised federal match to 80% for covering states): 7.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $22.1B gross, federal share ≈ $16.5B. HRSA Community Metabolic Health Program: free oral Wegovy or generic liraglutide at FQHCs and rural health clinics for uninsured and underinsured adults with BMI ≥30. Novo has a flat $149/month federal contract at any dose. 3.5M × $149 × 12 ≈ $6.3B a year, which equals the program's $19B three-year appropriation (FY2031–33). Enrolment is capped, and waitlists run 6–14 weeks in Texas, Florida and Georgia.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $4–30 a month across 100+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide analogues are sold widely in Southeast Asia, Latin America and the Gulf. Brazil and Canada have domestic generic semaglutide. India and China supply most of the world's incretin volume, and the US-to-India cash price gap is now ~30–40×.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline continued. In Jan 2032, TrumpRx maintenance prices fell again (Wegovy pill maintenance $249 → $199; Foundayo $149–229; injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $249–299; MariTide cash $279). Starting oral doses stay $149. Brands hold $149–299 in negotiated channels. The exception is Lilly's tirzepatide/bimagrumab combination (Zepbound Forte, Apr 2032): a $1,690 list price (the high figure), $599 cash through LillyDirect, and commercial formularies only with PA. ~0.4M users by Dec 2032. Medicare does not cover it, because bimagrumab has no dementia or CV claim. Employer coverage for weight management is down to 34%. Another ~11% cover only through metabolic tracks (~5.0M enrollees, all inside the 13.5M commercial users). Some employers dropped coverage for over-60 retirees, citing the Medicare dementia route. Orals are ~52% of users, driven by HRSA's oral-only formulary. Class now shows in the molecule more than in whether someone is on a drug at all: HRSA and Medicaid users mostly take oral semaglutide; Medicare users take tirzepatide; commercial and cash users take retatrutide, MariTide and the Forte combo. The gray market regrew from 5.2M to ~8.5M. 503A pharmacies in Florida, Texas and Arizona sell 'personalised' semaglutide-glycine, tirzepatide-B6 and compounded retatrutide through telehealth longevity brands. Telegram shops sell 'research' amycretin and fake 'muscle-sparing' add-on vials, mostly follistatin peptides and SARMs, since bimagrumab is an antibody and hard to counterfeit.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Aug 2031)
GLP-1/GIP agonist plus activin type II receptor antibody combination: weekly tirzepatide co-packaged with monthly subcutaneous bimagrumab (Zepbound Forte, approved Apr 2032)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD, and since Jul 2031 in adults 60+ with obesity without CVD (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial ongoing)
alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide, Dec 2031), the first approved compulsive-behaviour indication
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' and longevity microdosing by lean adults 35–65 without obesity, cash or compounded, sold by longevity clinics in Scottsdale, Miami, Austin and Manhattan
gambling-disorder treatment, including a Massachusetts Gaming Commission–funded pilot that pays for oral semaglutide through problem-gambling treatment providers
compulsive shopping, pornography and screen-use reduction via telehealth
dementia-prevention use by 50–59-year-olds below the label's age floor, cash-paid
microdosing for 'steadiness' at work, now publicly discouraged by most large HR departments but still common
semaglutide in under-12s with severe obesity (off-label)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Amycretin (filed Oct 2029, under review at the start of the step) was approved Aug 2031 at ~22% weight loss and mostly sits on commercial formularies. The muscle-preserving driver is realised by Lilly's tirzepatide/bimagrumab combination. Bimagrumab adjuncts were in phase 3 with no filing stated. Lilly filed the BLA in Feb 2031 on phase 3 data showing ~25% weight loss with ~90% of it fat mass (vs ~70% on tirzepatide alone). The FDA approved it Apr 2032, 14 months after filing. The label claims lean-mass preservation by DXA, not fracture or functional benefit, but the marketing ('lose the weight, keep the strength') implies both. Retatrutide remains limited to 9 mg for most patients. MariTide is used mostly in employer clinics. No implant exists (programmes still phase 1/2). No US generic semaglutide or tirzepatide: patent settlements put first US generic entry after 2032. Oral semaglutide's AUD phase 3 read out positive in Feb 2031, the sNDA was filed in May 2031 with priority review, and approval came Dec 2031. Gambling-disorder phase 3 trials (semaglutide; tirzepatide) are enrolling and report no earlier than 2034. Global incretin market ~$165B (2031). US net prices are drifting down ~4–6% a year.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Since the exocrine signal, chronic diarrhoea in long-term users now triggers faecal elastase testing instead of being dismissed. Bimagrumab adds diarrhoea and muscle spasms in the combination.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged. Combination and retatrutide users show the highest rates.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation now runs mainly on exocrine insufficiency.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; the post-2029 filings citing EPI are consolidated in a new MDL (2031).

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after >2 years, and ~1.45 in people who have cycled three or more times. The dementia-route expansion quadrupled the number of 65+ users at the highest absolute risk. The Forte combination preserves DXA lean mass, but there are no fracture or bone-density outcome data. Its phase 3 showed no bone-mineral-density benefit over tirzepatide alone.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (Jul 2028) retained. Forte label carries the lean-mass claim with a 'no demonstrated fracture benefit' limitation statement. FTC opened an inquiry (Oct 2032) into 'frailty solved' advertising.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A pooled FDA Sentinel and Medicare analysis (~2.1M users) published Sep 2031, consistent with Danish and Korean registries, puts NAION at ~2.4 per 10,000 person-years in users 60+ vs ~1.1 in matched controls (HR ~2.2), highest in the first 18 months and after dose escalation. It runs across semaglutide and tirzepatide; data are thinner for newer agents. With ~16–17M users over 60, that implies roughly 2,000 excess cases a year, mostly permanent partial vision loss in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning in Warnings and Precautions (Nov 2031) for all incretin agonists. It advises baseline eye examination for users 60+ or with crowded optic discs, and discontinuation after NAION in one eye. CMS added a Part D-linked eye-exam code. The FAA issued guidance requiring an ophthalmology report for pilots starting incretins.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the AUD trial population.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The oral semaglutide AUD phase 3 is the first randomised trial to measure anhedonia systematically. It found clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~6% on drug vs ~2.5% on placebo at 52 weeks. Observational cohorts still show ~7–8% in users overall and ~10% on retatrutide. It is dose-related and mostly resolves within weeks of dose reduction or a holiday.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Anhedonia now appears in the adverse-reactions section of the oral semaglutide AUD label (Dec 2031). The FDA postmarketing observational study continues, and there is no class labelling.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Short planned drug holidays (1–3 weeks) show little regain, so they are now openly recommended for flatness. Regain after the Forte combination is mostly fat, and the muscle gain reverses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy framing and adherence monitoring.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency are consistently documented in low-intake users. Fat-soluble vitamin deficiency is linked to the exocrine signal. Lean longevity microdosers, already low in body fat, show unexpected iron and B12 deficiency.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language added to semaglutide and tirzepatide labels (2031).

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The semaglutide signal (~4.1 vs ~1.9 per 1,000 person-years after 5+ years) holds in a third cohort (UK CPRD, 2031). First tirzepatide data at 5–6 years show a similar but less precise excess. Reversibility is partial: faecal elastase recovers in about half of patients within a year of stopping.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EPI added to semaglutide Warnings and Precautions (Mar 2031). EMA PRAC recommended class labelling (2031); the FDA class decision for tirzepatide is pending its confirmatory analysis.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. The first pediatric liraglutide bone-density interim (2032, n≈1,100) showed slightly lower bone-mineral-density gain than expected at 2 years, within normal range and not yet interpretable. Lean adults using the drugs for longevity have no outcome data at all.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth postmarketing requirements continue. No requirement covers non-obese off-label users.

safety_ledger.effect: Bimagrumab adjunct effects (muscle spasms, acne, diarrhoea; unknown long-term effects of activin-receptor blockade)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Muscle spasms in ~30% and acne in ~12% in phase 3, mostly transient. Activin signalling also affects reproduction and haematology, and there are no long-term data. Gray-market 'muscle add-on' vials sold as bimagrumab equivalents are mostly SARMs or follistatin peptides, linked to liver-injury reports.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Forte label includes contraception advice and a 5-year postmarketing safety study. The FDA issued warning letters to 14 online sellers of 'muscle-sparing' add-ons (2032).

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~23,000 by late 2032. Compounded retatrutide from 503A pharmacies has been linked to dosing errors (mg/unit confusion) and to a 2032 cluster of 61 hospitalisations for severe vomiting and dehydration in Florida. Poison-centre calls are ~5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letters plus Florida and Texas pharmacy-board actions against 503A 'personalised' compounders (Jun 2032). Enforcement is still state-by-state and slow, and personal importation remains largely unenforced.

food_and_beverage.state: About 40% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~11–13% from 2025, sugary drinks ~10%. The subsidy reached the households that had held volume, so value-pack and private-label snack volumes in lower-income zip codes fell for the first time (~4% in 2032). Dollar General and Walmart cut snack shelf space in Texas and Georgia stores. Protein lines are now mass-market. Nestlé and Conagra launched 'Forte-ready' high-leucine meals, and whey prices remain elevated. Hershey and Mondelez continue SKU cuts and lean on international growth.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~13% from 2025, beer ~8%. The Dec 2031 AUD approval moved heavy-drinker treatment from off-label to labelled. State Medicaid programs and EAPs now pay for it, and the heaviest 10% of drinkers, who buy the bulk of volume, are the target population. Diageo and Brown-Forman cut further US distillery capacity. Non-alcoholic and functional-beverage lines grow. Bar closures spread from Midwestern mid-sized cities to Gulf Coast casino towns.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Small plates and protein menus are standard. Casual-dining check sizes keep falling. QSR value menus in lower-income markets softened as HRSA users ate less. Chains are piloting 'half-portion pricing'. Biloxi and Atlantic City buffets keep closing.

apparel.state: Plus-size retail keeps contracting, and Torrid announced another round of closures. The top tier buys structured athletic wear tailored for 'Forte' bodies with muscle and little fat. Resale and stretch serve cyclers and holiday-takers. Mid-market brands added 'between sizes' lines for people whose weight swings with dose holidays.

fitness.state: Strength training and body-composition scanning keep growing in mass-market gyms (Planet Fitness racks, budget DXA chains). Premium clubs face a pitch problem: if a pen preserves muscle, why pay $300 a month to lift? Equinox-style clubs rebranded around 'function' (grip strength, VO2max, balance) and fall-prevention programmes for dementia-route seniors. Premium membership growth slowed to low single digits.

insurance.state: Employer coverage for weight management is down to 34%. Some firms carve out retirees over 60 to the Medicare dementia route. Pharmacy trend ~+6%. Part D base premiums rose ~9% for 2032, with CMS citing incretin spend, and several standalone PDPs exited high-uptake regions. Adherence-conditioned wellness differentials persist under the 2027 guidance, but after the EEOC finding fewer firms publicise them. Medicaid budgets in the 12 new-coverage states absorb the 20% state share, ~$1.4B combined.

pharma.state: Lilly leads on tirzepatide's Medicare dementia volume, retatrutide and the Forte launch. Novo's growth runs through the HRSA flat-price contract, the AUD label and Medicaid. Volume rises faster than revenue because net prices fall. Amgen (MariTide) is entrenched in employer clinics. Boehringer is in MASH. Novo amycretin is new. Litigation and anti-counterfeiting costs run high, now including suits against 503A compounders. Indian and Chinese makers dominate volume outside the US.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Body shape still reads as income, but by molecule now rather than by being on or off a drug. A lean body with dense muscle and no visible effort reads as Forte, meaning commercial coverage or $599 cash. A lean, soft, slightly hollow body reads as HRSA or Medicaid oral semaglutide. A thin older body with a cane reads as the Medicare dementia route. In Austin and Charlotte, 'earned' muscle (calloused hands, a lifting history) became the new status marker once muscle could be bought.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The class uniform is still muscle, and its meaning is contested. Upper-tier Austin and Manhattan circles distinguish 'pen muscle' from 'bar muscle' and post grip-strength numbers alongside DXA. In McAllen, Texas, and rural Georgia, HRSA clinic lines made thin bodies common among cafeteria workers and home health aides for the first time. Ex-regainers in the bottom third are back on drug, thinner but not stronger. Lean Scottsdale and Miami professionals in their 40s microdose for 'metabolic age' scores, so thinness is no longer evidence of a drug or its absence. Upper-income children remain the most medicated pediatric cohort, but Medicaid EPSDT is narrowing that gap.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter. 'Holiday meals' have returned in a literal sense: families schedule dose skips around Thanksgiving and birthdays so the person who skipped can taste the meal. The 'Bread Alone' fasting church network claims ~650 congregations and now runs free-meal-and-fast nights next to HRSA clinics in Oklahoma. Protein etiquette has spread down-market.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps still carry 'lean-mass verified' badges, but 'Forte' bodies have made them less informative. A new 'on a holiday this week' status sells as a premium filter. Desire mismatch remains a common therapy complaint. Couples now openly time weekly-dose skips or switch off monthly MariTide to regain flexibility.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is widely discussed as something you can turn back on. 'Taking a holiday' is ordinary speech for wanting pleasure back for a weekend. For HRSA users appetite is the thing the free pill took away. Unmuted argues the subsidy medicated the poor without giving them the muscle. MAHA-aligned legislators attack the HRSA program as 'pharma welfare', while their older constituents fill dementia-route prescriptions.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~6% on drug vs ~2.5% on placebo in the AUD RCT, and ~7–8% in observational cohorts, ~10% on retatrutide. Surveys (KFF, 2032) find ~38% of current users report 'flatness' at some point, and ~45% of users have taken at least one planned drug holiday or dose step-down for mood, pleasure or sex in the past year.
interior_life.framing: It is called 'the flatness' or 'going flat', a known, nameable, adjustable side effect, like drowsiness on antihistamines. Clinicians speak of 'titrating for feeling'. HR dropped 'steadiness' from competency language after the 2031 EEOC finding. The AUD label made blunting official for one product, and the compulsive-behaviour indications make some users read it as the mechanism rather than a bug.
interior_life.effect_on_work: In Aug 2031 the EEOC issued a reasonable-cause finding in one of the two long-pending ADA charges against a Columbus-corridor logistics firm, citing promotion patterns tied to metabolic-track adherence. Most large employers removed 'even under pressure' language and stopped reporting adherence beside safety metrics. Metabolic tracks still hold ~5.0M enrollees, and clinic-administered MariTide still records every dose. Employees increasingly ask clinics for 'holiday weeks', and some clinics grant them under a documented-holiday policy that keeps the premium differential. Financial traders and sales teams openly time holidays before quarter-ends 'to get hungry'.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off nights', once Unmuted events in Detroit and Baltimore, have gone commercial. Promoters in Chicago and Atlanta advertise 'holiday weekend' club nights. Flat fiction is now a shelf category, and a hit 2032 HBO comedy is set in a family where everyone is on a different dose schedule. Sportsbook handle per active account fell further, and Massachusetts's semaglutide gambling pilot is in DraftKings's investor risk disclosures. Comedians do 'going flat' bits the way an earlier generation did Prozac.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Planned drug holidays came back, aided by orals' daily flexibility and weekly injectables. Monthly MariTide users increasingly switch to weekly products for this reason. Couples therapists report fewer 'parallel lives' and more negotiation over holiday calendars. Partners argue over whose turn it is to go off.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The coverage fight moved from employers to the budget. Republican and Democratic budget hawks target the Part D premium increase, and the HRSA program's 2033 reauthorisation is the next fight. Older voters on the dementia route are a large new constituency for keeping coverage. The MAHA wing is split between attacking 'pharma welfare' and defending seniors' prescriptions. Gaming-state legislators (Nevada, New Jersey) quietly lobby against expanding gambling-disorder coverage. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence. 2032 turnout among 65+ was normal.

state.regulatory_posture: The FDA kept its pro-speed posture (amycretin, Forte, the AUD sNDA under priority review, the tirzepatide dementia extension) while acting on safety: the NAION class warning, semaglutide EPI labelling, micronutrient labelling. Enforcement against compounders is delegated in practice to state pharmacy boards. Florida and Texas acted in 2032, and Arizona has not. The FTC opened an inquiry into 'frailty solved' advertising.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The Mar 2031 bipartisan health package (PBM reform plus extenders) created the HRSA Community Metabolic Health Program. It appropriates $19B over FY2031–33 to buy oral Wegovy at a flat $149/month and generic liraglutide for free dispensing at FQHCs and rural clinics, and it raised the Medicaid federal match to 80% for states covering obesity drugs. It did not create a Medicare obesity benefit. Medicare expansion came through the Jul 2031 tirzepatide label and CMS's Part D guidance. Public payers now cover ~41% of users.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: HRSA program enrolment requires consent to refill tracking and 90-day check-ins, and it disenrolls patients after two missed refills. Waitlisted patients take their slots. The tri-agency 30% adherence differential stands. Clinic records for monthly injections still flow to wellness vendors. Three state Medicaid programmes condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. CMS's eye-exam code creates a new data stream linked to Part D fills.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE rules are unchanged, and the Army recruit oral pilot continues. After the NAION warning, the FAA requires an ophthalmology report for pilots starting incretins. DOT still has not ruled on drivers using drugs for alcohol reduction, which is now on-label after the AUD approval. Trucking associations want a ruling.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply most of the world's incretin volume. US–India trade talks produced a 2032 side letter on pharmacy-export data sharing without effective mail enforcement. Novo's $149 federal contract is cited by Danish politicians as proof that US prices were always negotiable. The FDA is dispute-checking Chinese API suppliers to US 503A compounders.

events.event: Congress passes a bipartisan health package that funds $19B over three years for free oral Wegovy and generic liraglutide at community health centres, under a flat $149-a-month federal contract with Novo, and raises Medicaid matching to 80% for states that cover obesity drugs; within a year 12 more states sign on
events.driver: state_action: subsidy; coverage_shift: public_expansion; price_path: managed_decline

events.event: FDA extends tirzepatide's dementia-risk-reduction claim to adults 60 and over with obesity but without heart disease; CMS tells Part D plans to limit prior authorisation to age and BMI checks, and Medicare's dementia-route users climb from 1.6M to 6.5M by late 2032

FDA adds a class warning for NAION to all incretin-agonist labels after a Sentinel–Medicare analysis of 2.1M users finds optic-nerve stroke risk roughly doubled in users over 60, recommending baseline eye exams; the FAA follows with pilot guidance

FDA approves oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder, the first compulsive-behaviour indication for an incretin; the label is the first to list anhedonia as an adverse reaction, months after the EEOC found reasonable cause in a Columbus logistics firm's adherence-linked promotions

FDA approves Lilly's Zepbound Forte, weekly tirzepatide co-packaged with monthly bimagrumab, 14 months after its February 2031 filing, on data showing ~25% weight loss with lean mass preserved; launched at a $1,690 list price and $599 cash under the tagline 'lose the weight, keep the strength'

Florida and Texas pharmacy boards act against 503A compounders selling 'personalised' retatrutide and semaglutide blends through longevity telehealth brands after 61 hospitalisations in a Florida cluster; the FDA warns 14 online sellers of fake 'muscle-sparing' add-ons

open_tensions: Medicare is now the default payer for older users through a dementia-prevention claim whose confirmatory trial has not read out. The same population carries the new NAION class warning, the fracture warning and the longest exposure to the exocrine signal, and Part D premiums are rising on the bill.

The HRSA free-provision program runs out of appropriation in FY2033 with waitlists in the South. If it lapses, ~3.5M of the poorest users face abrupt discontinuation and regain, the pattern the gray market has already shown.

Muscle is now for sale (Zepbound Forte at $599) on a label that claims lean mass, not fracture protection. Meanwhile subsidised users get the oral that thins without preserving muscle, so the drug class reproduces the body hierarchy that public coverage was meant to flatten.

Drug holidays are now mainstream practice for the flatness, while employers' clinic-administered monthly doses, the 30% adherence differential and HRSA's refill-based disenrolment all penalise the gaps that holidays create.

prose.headline: Free Pills for the Poor, Muscle in a Pen for the Rich, and a Dose Skipped for Birthday Cake: Medicare's Weight Decade Begins
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 almost one American adult in four takes an incretin drug, about sixty-two million people, and nearly a third have tried one. The bigger change is who pays. For the first time the largest payer is public. Medicare did not get an obesity benefit; Congress never reopened that. It got one indirectly. In July 2031 the FDA extended tirzepatide's dementia-prevention claim to anyone over sixty with obesity, and CMS told Part D plans to stop making doctors fight for it. Six and a half million older Americans now take a weight drug as dementia prevention. Part D premiums rose nine percent in 2032 and nobody in Washington will say why out loud.

The poor arrived through a different door. In March 2031 a health package that was mostly about pharmacy middlemen also bought Novo's pill at a flat $149 a month and handed it out free at community health centres. Three and a half million people take it, from cafeteria workers in McAllen to home aides in rural Georgia. The money runs out in 2033 and the waitlists already run three months. A dozen more states joined Medicaid coverage once Washington offered to pay four-fifths. Among the bottom third of earners, use went from one in eight to one in five.

The gap in who takes the drugs narrowed. The gap in what the drugs do to the body widened. The free pill thins people without strengthening them. In April Lilly launched Zepbound Forte, tirzepatide paired with a monthly antibody that keeps muscle on while fat comes off. It costs $599 a month in cash and is advertised as the end of frailty. The label claims lean mass, not stronger bones or fewer falls, and the FTC has started asking about the gap. In Austin, where muscle once proved you had a coach and a scanner, people now ask whether yours came from a barbell or a pen.

Safety moved forward and nothing collapsed. In November 2031 the FDA put a class warning on every incretin for a rare optic-nerve stroke that roughly doubles in users over sixty. In a population this old and this large, that means a couple of thousand people a year losing part of the sight in one eye. Seniors now get an eye exam with their first fill. The pancreatic-enzyme problem found in Danish long-term users is on semaglutide's label, and the decision on tirzepatide is pending.

The flatness is no longer a secret or a selling point. The alcohol-use-disorder trial that won oral semaglutide its first compulsion indication in December 2031 measured lost pleasure under randomisation and found it. That label is the first to list it. Months earlier the EEOC had found reasonable cause against a Columbus logistics firm that promoted the adherent. Employers dropped the word 'steadiness'. People started talking about the flatness the way their parents talked about Prozac, and they treat it the same way: lower the dose, or take a week off. Nearly half of users took a planned holiday last year, for a wedding, a quarter-end or a lover. Monthly shots are losing ground to weekly ones because weekly is easier to skip.

Outside every rule there is a second market, larger than before. Florida and Arizona compounders sell 'personalised' retatrutide blends through longevity brands to lean forty-somethings chasing a metabolic age. Telegram shops sell fake muscle add-ons. Eight and a half million people buy outside the regulated channels. State pharmacy boards act one at a time.

No one would call it a crisis. Snack aisles shrank again, this time in the dollar stores. Fewer people bet on Sunday, and casino-town bars keep closing. Grandparents skip a dose so they can taste the birthday cake. The country is thinner, older on the drug, and paying for it together.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Kowalczyk wakes at six in Toledo because the cat does. Sunday. Her pen is in the butter compartment, where it has been since Medicare started paying in January: $47 a month, dementia-risk code, which her doctor typed while saying the word 'prevention' twice.

She doesn't take it today. Mason turns nine on Wednesday, and Denise wants to taste the cake. Dr. Patel calls it a holiday. Her sister calls it cheating.

The drops from Tuesday's eye exam have worn off, but the leaflet is still on the counter: OPTIC NERVE, in a box. The ophthalmologist said her discs looked fine. She keeps rereading 'one eye' anyway.

At church the pastor's wife is visibly smaller since August. She gets her pills free at the clinic on Dorr Street and says she waited eleven weeks. Her arms are loose at the elbow, the same as Denise's.

On the TV in the narthex a silver-haired man does a pull-up. Lose the weight. Keep the strength. $599. Denise pays $47. She does the math every time the ad runs.

Her son-in-law Ray comes over for lunch. He buys something called reta from a man in Perrysburg, and he eats half a sandwich and calls it plenty. He's laughing more lately. Kayla says that's because he's been off for nine days. 'Off for a while,' Ray says, and winks at nobody.

In the evening Denise makes pierogi. She eats four. She tastes the onions, all of them, and cries a little at the stove, not from sadness. Wednesday she'll go back on.
